extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, librarians, researchers, and general readers seeking information about the zbMATH Open bibliographic/reviewing service
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive overview of the zbMATH Open abstracting and reviewing service for mathematics, including its coverage, history, access model, and how reviews are produced and organized. Useful for readers evaluating or locating mathematical literature and bibliographic resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access / Cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Access: Cost: Open access. As of January 2021, the complete database is accessible for free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously only the first three records in a search were available without a subscription; since Jan 2021 the whole database is open (page notes archived announcements on zbmath.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplines / Subject scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage: Disciplines: Pure mathematics, applied mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service provides reviews and abstracts for articles in mathematics and related areas; it uses Mathematics Subject Classification codes for organising reviews by topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record depth / Content types
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstracting service provides reviews (brief accounts of contents) of current articles, conference papers, books and other publications; reviews are predominantly in English with occasional entries in German and French.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Format coverage: Journal articles, Conference papers, Books (and other publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zentralblatt/zbMATH reviews more than 2,300 journals and serials worldwide, as well as books and conference proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporal coverage: 1868–present (infobox notes first entry from 1755); older issues incorporated back to 1826 in earlier digital efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The database incorporated the 200,000 entries of the earlier Jahrbuch (1868–1942) and since 2004 older issues were incorporated back to 1826; electronic service (zbMATH) has been available since 1996.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of records / Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: No. of records: more than 4 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale indicators also include incorporation of 200,000 Jahrbuch entries and ongoing review coverage across thousands of journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update frequency / Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically print issues were published as soon as sufficiently many reviews were available (three or four weeks); the electronic service has enabled more frequent updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Languages: English, French, German; reviews are predominantly in English with occasional entries in German and French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multilingual review content reflects historical and international contributions; most contemporary reviews are in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection / Review authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are volunteers invited by the editors based on their published work or a recommendation by an existing reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are written by mathematicians worldwide; selection is editor-driven and relies on demonstrated expertise or recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational/Editorial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer / Editors: European Mathematical Society, FIZ Karlsruhe, and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences; distributed by Springer (historically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service is produced by the Berlin office of FIZ Karlsruhe – Leibniz Institute for Information Infrastructure GmbH and edited jointly with EMS and the Heidelberg Academy; distribution and production history affect presentation and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of classification scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses the Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes for organising reviews by topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC codes are employed to categorize and allow topical navigation/search of reviews and abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reviewed sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The service reviews more than 2,300 journals and serials worldwide, as well as books and conference proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates breadth of source coverage and signals that the database aims to be comprehensive across major mathematical publication venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery formats / Platform availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided both over the Web and historically in printed form; the printed issue was discontinued in 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic access (zbMATH from 1996) and earlier INKA-MATH presence mean digital search and retrieval are primary; print ceased in 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical completeness vs timeliness tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical note: the Jahrbuch aimed for documentary completeness (only published after all papers in a year were processed), which reduced timeliness; Zentralblatt prioritized speed of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrast explains editorial choices between completeness and rapid availability of reviews and informs users about historical strengths/weaknesses of the aggregated content.
